chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyyah, from Khaythamah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is free from His creation, and His creation is free from Him. Whatever falls under the name of 'thing' other than Allah, the Mighty and High, is created. And Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of all things.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is free from His creation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to resolve the theological debate on whether Allah is a 'thing' (shay') by distinguishing between the created essence of the universe and the uncreated essence of the Creator. It affirms that while all contingent beings are 'things' distinct from God, Allah remains the sole, uncreated Agent (Fa'il) whose essence is not limited by the attributes of creation. This establishes the foundation for divine simplicity (tawhid al-dhat) in Shia creed, ensuring that God's existence is not conflated with the multiplicity of the cosmos.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-`Alawi (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of `Ali ibn `Atiyyah, on the authority of Khaythamah that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is free from His Creation, and His Creation is free from Him. Whatever can be defined by the word “thing” is a creation other than Allah, the Mighty and High. Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of all things.
